meta.title: American Crusade: Our Fight to Stay Free
meta.author: Pete Hegseth

parts.title: Our American Crusade: Rallying Against the Left

sentences: **"Our American Crusade"** delves into the deep **political divide** in America after the **2016 election**, drawing on a historical narrative to rally support against **leftist ideologies** blamed for undermining the nation's **soul and institutions**.
The author calls for an **American Crusade**, likening it to historical **crusades and revolutions** as a defense against what is perceived as an existential threat posed by the Left.
The piece contrasts two immigrant perspectives, highlighting a divergence in **patriotism and gratitude** towards America.
It emphasizes **extreme loyalty** and champions **Trump’s presidency** as critical for preserving America's essence.
Initially, **Pete Hegseth** dismissed **Donald Trump's** "America first" slogan as isolationism, reminding him of the **America First Committee** before **WWII**.
**Hegseth** believed it lacked foreign policy substance.
Yet, with **Trump's** nomination, **Hegseth's** stance changed, recognizing "America first" as pivotal for **US** actions, ensuring **US strength** amidst global threats.
**Trump's** presidency emphasized evaluating actions through an **America-first** lens, challenging elitists while resonating with patriots.
**Americanism** emerges as **Hegseth's** antidote to leftism, centering on the **US founding ideals**.
**Americanism** is defined as allegiance to individual freedom and equal justice, aligning with **American nationalism**.
The enemies of **America** attack these ideas, perverting nationalism as **racist** to undermine **national sovereignty**.
Exploring history and inherent human flaws, **Hegseth** stresses **Americanism** as the cornerstone of progress, from historical **civil rights advancements** to modern technological developments.
The challenges lie in preserving core principles, crucial against **leftist** cultural and policy attacks.

parts.title: Founding Documents and Ideals vs. Leftist Agenda

sentences: ## American Ideals vs. Leftist Reality
The **difference** between the **Declaration of Independence** and the **Constitution** is crucial.
While both are linked, the **Declaration** provides America’s **soul,** proclaiming principles like **God-given** rights and the **right to alter** government.
In contrast, the **Constitution** offers the **structure** to uphold those ideals.
**Leftists** disregard the **Declaration**, seeking a **“living Constitution”** that can justify their control and suppress freedoms like the **Second Amendment**.
American founders ensured **checks** against majority rule to protect individual rights.
Contrastingly, leftists crave "**democracy**" to quickly reshape society.

**Current cultural conflict** in the US Democratic party signals a **struggle between older political power**, represented by figures like **Nancy Pelosi**, and the **rising influence of leftist figures** like **AOC and Bernie Sanders**.
While Pelosi has **votes in Congress**, she lacks the appeal of the **younger audience** who resonate with socialist rhetoric.
This is seen as a **cultural shift** where today's political establishment might not represent the **soul of tomorrow**.
The conversation on **leftism versus individual freedom** highlights the belief that **collectivism and outdated welfare policies** don't work, exemplified by the **Soviet Union's collapse**.
Critics argue that a **government-centered approach** stifles personal initiative and that **true empowerment lies** in personal freedom and entrepreneurship.
The **failures of socialistic systems** point out that despite good intentions, **overreliance on government** leads to inefficiencies and fosters a **state of dependency**.

parts.title: NATO's Role and Criticism in Afghanistan

sentences: When I served in **Afghanistan** under a **NATO mission**, I was with the **International Security Assistance Force (ISAF)**.
Wearing an **American flag** on one shoulder and an **ISAF patch** on the other became a joke; as other troops from **fifty countries** rarely engaged in combat compared to **US troops**.
At **ISAF headquarters in Kabul** it was clear this was "**the United States’s war**" with little support from allies.
Their **political limitations** on the battlefield meant others did not or could not fight.
NATO seemed more like a **defense arrangement for Europe**, funded largely by the **US**, rather than a true alliance.
In **Afghanistan**, it felt like **America** was alone in combat, and the larger **NATO alliance** did little when **Russia**, led by **Putin**, invaded **Crimea**.
Today's **NATO** seems like a distraction, with **European countries** not interested in rebuilding **militaries** post-**World War II**.
**Critics** argue it's still essential in dealing with an aggressive **Russia**, claiming **NATO** is vital for like-minded countries.
But the perception on the ground was its limitations and the disparity in **combat contributions**.
**Socialism** is equated to taxing hard-working individuals more, redistributing their earnings to others via **government control**.
The **author** argues that socialism could allure young people due to misleading notions of "economic justice".
Schools might not highlight **capitalism's merits** while presenting **socialist ideas** favorably, driving a false narrative of fairness interpreted by politicians and educators.
A **discussion** with **Gunner** uses **rubber duckies** to illustrate issues like excessive production and overpricing affecting supply and demand.
The talk evolves into **political economy**, observing how **governments** impact businesses and ultimately skew a free-market system towards **socialism**.

paragraphs.heading: Elitism and Political Correctness
sentences: Vice President-elect Pence called Pete Hegseth to arrange a meeting with President-elect Trump, considering him for a role as **Secretary of Veterans Affairs**.
Despite Pete's previous criticism of Trump, his advocacy for veterans' issues had caught Trump's attention.
During the meeting at Trump Tower, Trump humorously referenced Pete's earlier support for **Marco Rubio**, nicknaming him "Little Marco."
Pete then complimented Trump on his nickname for Elizabeth Warren, **"Pocahontas"**, and Trump explained his reasoning as a marketer.
Trump's comments and approach highlight his strategy against **political correctness**, which he believes limits free speech and maintains power for an elite class.
The **elites** are seen as those who think they are better than others, using complex language to confuse and control.
The **media** and **tech oligarchies** are criticized for promoting **left-wing** ideologies and silencing **conservatives**.
The **hypocrisy** of the **elites**, who want control through **political correctness**, is highlighted.
When people are silenced or censored, like on **social media**, it's viewed as controlling speech to maintain elite power.
The speaker encourages **laughing** at and **mocking** these controls to regain freedom.
Rejecting **elitism** and political correctness is argued for, viewing them as forms of **authoritarianism**.
It promotes **free speech** and questioning the narrative pushed by elites, urging people to follow **Trump's example** in standing against elitist values.
Emphasizing **American values** and unity is contrasted against the divisive nature of political correctness.
Empowering the "real elite," everyday Americans, against what is perceived as **elitist ridicule** is called for.

parts.title: Understanding Esmatullah's Beliefs & The Threat of Islamism

sentences: **Esmatullah** was an interpreter in **Afghanistan** during the author's deployment.
Although **Esmat** was a regular **Muslim**, not a **radical Islamist**, he believed that **Islam** would rule the world due to high birth rates.
**Islamism**, derived from the **Quran**, is perceived as a significant threat to freedom, being aggressive and evangelical.
Many **Westerners** mistakenly view **Islam** as a "religion of peace," overlooking the aggressive nature of **Islamism**.
In reality, while **peaceful Muslims** exist, **Islamism** seeks the domination of **Islamic** ideals globally.
**Islamism** uses the beliefs of moderate **Muslims** to spread its **radical agenda**.
Despite the presence of non-radical **Muslims**, **Islamism** is deeply rooted in the core teachings of **Islam**, making it difficult to separate from the **moderate interpretation**.
Islamists aim to impose **Islam** on others, a mission reflecting **Muhammad’s** life and Quranic teachings.
This poses a challenge as Islam doesn't have a "New Testament" equivalent, meaning no substantial reform shift akin to **Christianity's transformation**.
Therefore, **Islamism** is not just religious but also a political system incompatible with any other.
With **Saudi Arabian** funding, groups like the **Muslim Brotherhood** advance **Islamist missions**, posing significant challenges to Western freedoms.

parts.title: The Evolution and Defense of Western Civilization

sentences: **Western civilization** is viewed through the prism of **Christianity's** evolution and the **ongoing battles** it has faced.
Initially, Christianity spread peacefully but, due to **persecution**, took a militaristic stance under **Constantine the Great**.
**Christianity** and **Islam** are contrasted, noting that while Christianity initially propagated through love and faith, **Islam** spread through **jihad and warfare**.
By the **11th century**, the imminent threat from **Islam** led to the **Crusades** as a defensive measure to protect **Christian faith and territories**.
The piece also argues that leftists today would argue for "diplomacy" much like peaceful negotiations, ignoring the **historical necessity** of the **Crusades**.

Leftists are portrayed as unwilling to accept the value of what **Crusaders** accomplished for the **modern world**, such as preserving **Western civilization** and ultimately enabling phenomena like the **Protestant Reformation** and the **Renaissance**.
This sets the stage for the "American Crusade," encouraging readers to fight for **Christian and American values**.
